items.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001
items.q: I would go and hear Carmen McRae and she was very, very open, so I could ask her a lot of different questions about how she was approaching songs... and you know she would tell me.

ctx.x: Do they ever feel pressured by instrumentalists to really, you know you better know your stuff here?

Well I think my uncle just always wanted me to be prepared. I guess they do, but my uncle always wanted me to be ready and be prepared, be able to communicate clearly my ideas and specifically what it was that I wanted to hear or what I wanted. And so that was the training early on. And you know I would go and I would listen to other vocalists too. Because at the time there was not a lot of, there weren’t a lot of schools for jazz, to study jazz music. So the way that you got it was through experience and through…

There’s a certain amount of physicalization that you do. When I think back of when I saw Betty Carter, I can almost see a nice comparison there. Just, I don’t know, the way you use your arms. It works.
